primitives.name: Compliance Scan Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Claude API output (for whatever reason — model variance, prompt-injection by the input data, etc.) contains a banned phrase: ``` ## Cold open This week our AI-powered scoring engine caught some interesting market inefficiencies in MLB...
primitives.assumptions: Text is parsed into tokens; banned vocabulary is pre-defined in ruleset.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When any banned term is detected in input text.

layer2.mapping: Compliance scan maps to a Boolean-valued predicate over token sequences; equivalent to a language acceptor with forbidden substrings.
layer2.telemetry: Flag count per rule, final status code.

primitives.name: Editor UI Feedback Loop
primitives.verbatim_quote: Editor UI highlights the offending span ("AI-powered") inline in the markdown.
primitives.assumptions: UI supports inline annotation and replacement suggestions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: On detection of flagged text segment.

layer2.mapping: Feedback loop overlays semantic correction onto raw text; modeled as a controlled transformation T(text) → T'(text) where T' = T ∪ Suggestion.
layer2.telemetry: User interaction time, edit frequency, suggestion acceptance rate.

primitives.name: Publishing Constraint Enforcement
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Forbidden behavior - Editor MUST NOT publish a draft with red compliance status.
primitives.assumptions: Publishing is gated by compliance state; no silent bypass allowed.

layer2.mapping: Enforcement is a logical constraint: if status == red then action ≠ publish.
layer2.telemetry: Number of failed publish attempts, retraction events.

These form a closed-loop system where the output of one feeds into the input of another.
